items.title: Why the 'Lucky Generation' without mortgages is still dismayed by RBA rate hike
items.description: A third of Australians could benefit if banks raise deposit rates on savings, while mortgage holders are having to decide what to cut back on.

items.title: Liberals say $15b fund backing 'loser' green projects will fuel inflation
items.description: The government is loosening the rules of its $15 billion investment fund to allow it to back loss-making emissions reduction projects, which the Liberals say will further fuel inflation.

items.title: Ley stands by demand to exile Nats rebels amid talks on Coalition split
items.description: The Nationals leader has refused to disclose whether he will reject an offering for the Coalition to reunite with a list of conditions, including a six-month suspension from the frontbench for three Nationals senators.

items.title: Second Australian dies in Japan while skiing, local media reports
items.description: A second Australian has died in Japan, the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade has confirmed.

items.title: Government to sell historic defence properties
items.description: The Albanese government has identified 67 defence sites for potential sale, aiming to unlock up to $1.8 billion.

items.title: Melinda Gates glad to be 'away from the muck' after Epstein revelations
items.description: Melinda French Gates says her ex-husband, Bill Gates, needs to answer for his behaviour alleged in the latest batch of Epstein files.

items.title: Live: Clive Palmer announces High Court challenge against electoral donation cap
items.description: Clive Palmer has announced he will launch a High Court challenge against the validity of a cap on electoral donations. Follow live.

items.title: Breaking: Victorian MP quits, triggering by-election months out from state poll
items.description: Retired tennis star and former deputy Liberal leader Sam Groth will quit Victorian parliament next week, about a month after announcing he would not contest November's state election.

items.title: Live: ASX climbs after Wall Street's tech sell-off as bitcoin up above $US76,000
items.description: The Australian share market edges up after a brutal session on Wall Street, weighed down by massive losses in tech and AI stocks like Nvidia and Microsoft, while bitcoin trades above $76,000 after dropping to a 16-month low. Follow live.

items.title: The government has options to fight inflation, but most are unpopular
items.description: The federal government has a variety of options available if it wants to do more to stave off inflation, but none are popular.

items.title: Mental strength, decision making keys to family's stunning survival off WA
items.description: "Outback Mike" Atkinson says the Appelbee family's ability to stay calm and make smart decisions was critical to their survival after they were swept out to sea off Geographe Bay.

items.title: AI bots have created a religion, but experts say that's not the scary part
items.description: A social network run entirely by AI bots has attracted more than a million users — but experts warn it is not what the bots are saying that poses the true risk.

items.title: Trump tells Republicans 'we should take over the voting'
items.description: Donald Trump says he wants Republicans to "nationalise" US elections and has encouraged his party to "take over the voting" in at least some parts of the country.

items.title: First crewed mission around the Moon in 53 years delayed by leak
items.description: A hydrogen leak has pushed back NASA's plans to launch the Artemis II mission to send humans around the Moon to March, at the earliest.

items.title: Randa Abdel-Fattah to appear at Adelaide literary event in March
items.description: Palestinian Australian author, lawyer and activist Randa Abdel-Fattah will be appearing at the one-off literary event created to fill the void left by the cancellation of this year's Adelaide Writers' Week, organisers have announced.

items.title: High Court dismisses appeal from Eddie Obeid, son Moses, Ian Macdonald
items.description: The High Court throws out an appeal by former New South Wales Labor ministers Ian MacDonald and Eddie Obeid, and Mr Obeid's son Moses, after they were convicted for conspiring over a coal mine licence.

items.title: The three exhibitions you shouldn't miss around Australia this summer
items.description: From Aussie expat Ron Mueck's hyper-realistic sculptures and Icelandic Danish artist Olafur Eliasson's thought-provoking installations to the best contemporary artists in Tasmania, here are three exhibitions to see.

items.title: Former PMs and premiers farewell Dame Marie Bashir at state funeral
items.description: "Proud country girl" Dame Marie Bashir has been remembered by former prime ministers, premiers and family at a state funeral in Sydney.

items.title: Police tell teen caught driving at 189km/h: 'We're calling your parents'
items.description: The teenager on his P-plates was pulled over by police along a Sunshine Coast motorway driving at almost 200km/h.

items.title: No plans to increase security at Wittenoom after blogger's 'devastating' visit
items.description: Asbestos disease advocates criticise a Queensland blogger for taking her daughter to one of Australia's most contaminated sites.

items.title: Teen charged with rape and taking a person by force after Adelaide park incident
items.description: A 16-year-old boy is facing charges of rape and taking a person by force after the alleged sexual assault of another teenager in Adelaide's south on Saturday night, police say.

items.title: More than 140 alleged offenders linked to 'satanic' Sydney paedophile ring
items.description: Another man has been charged and a further 145 alleged offenders have been referred to international law enforcement agencies as part of an investigation into a satanic child sex abuse material ring.

items.title: Reality bites for Brisbane 2032 as 'dispersed' Games costs escalate
items.description: Brisbane 2032 president Andrew Liveris says the bid budget "bears no resemblance to reality" as the financial impact of a dispersed Olympics hits home.

items.title: NT residents feel less safe despite government's crime crackdown, report finds
items.description: A new report reveals NT residents felt less safe over the past year, despite a government crackdown on crime.

items.title: Up to 100,000 fish found dead at Lake Menindee
items.description: Residents of a far west New South Wales community found tens of thousands of dead fish on the banks of Lake Menindee.
